subject: Quantargo: request for uplifted uptime & latency guarantees - governance/questions
messages:
From: Kate Sullivan <kate@quantargo.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Tighter uptime/latency guarantees for pilot

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the routing and fallback behavior. We have an internal board discussion Friday and need to confirm whether Redwood can support a slightly more aggressive SLA for our pilot. High-level asks: 

- p95 response latency <= 80ms for text-gen in us-west region (steady-state, 1k rps sustained)
- 99.95% monthly uptime for the dedicated pool during our pilot months
- Geo failover plan within 60s for regional outage

We're prepared to sign a 6-month pilot commitment and a small reserved capacity commitment if we can lock these guardrails. I've attached a short PDF with their asks and the internal justification.

Can you advise next steps / whether this requires an internal carve-out? We may need runbook commitments and a statement on how Redwood will measure/monitor these numbers.

Cheers,
Kate Sullivan
Head of ML Platform, Quantargo
Quantargo Inc.
Attachment: quantargo-slo-request.pdf
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Sullivan <kate@quantargo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Tighter uptime/latency guarantees for pilot

Kate — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. We're excited by the opportunity. Quick summary of what I think we need from our side before committing: 

1) Product/Eng: confirm feasibility of sustained p95 <= 80ms at ~1k RPS on dedicated pool + quantization/profile expectations.
2) Infra/Ops: a documented failover runbook (demo of 60s flip) and monitoring/alerting thresholds.
3) Security/Compliance: confirm there are no additional data residency or audit constraints for the reserved pool.
4) Legal/Finance: outline payment/commitment terms and what a short-term SLA credit looks like.

Looping in Karthik (product) and Neha (ops) to get a feasibility read and an initial list of engineering ask items. We'll sync internally and aim to get back with a proposal by Tue 5/4 EOD.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantargo SLO asks — product + ops alignment

Team — forwarding Quantargo's ask. Quick priorities:

- Karthik: can we run a capacity/latency sim against the candidate model variants (base-7B quantized vs fp16 13B) and validate p95 at 1k rps on a small dedicated pool? If not, what's required (autoscale, instance size)?
- Neha: what would a 60s geo-failover look like operationally? Any special config (DNS TTLs, routing policies) we need to implement?
- Rafael: finance/legal will need a proposal template for a 6-month pilot with an uptime uplift and what credit/penalty structure we can offer. Keep it conservative — we can offer a buffer on credits until we have the runbook.

I attached a patch of our runbook template and a stub 'draft-moprunbook.md' for the pilot. Please reply with concrete asks (people + ETA).

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft-moprunbook.md
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quantargo SLO asks — product + ops alignment

Thanks — technical readout below after an initial assessment and a quick perf run on staging: 

- Feasibility: Achievable with current runtime if we run the fp16 13B variant on reserved c5/rtx-optimized nodes and enable KV prefix caching for steady traffic. The 7B quantized variant hits ~85-95ms p95 under load; to reach <=80ms we need either slightly larger instances or a higher reserved concurrency.
- Throughput: 1k sustained rps is borderline for a single pool; recommend a 2-node dedicated pool with autoscale headroom to absorb bursts.
- Failover: 60s geo failover is operationally possible if we pre-warm a warm-standby pool in us-east and use health-check driven routing with low DNS TTL (10s). Need to confirm with networking team for automated failover scripts.
- Observability: We can surface token-level latency and p95 per-route in the Console; for contractual measurement we should define a single canonical metric (api.p95_token_latency.us-west) and a measurement window.

Concrete asks from Eng/Ops: 
1) Approval to provision a 2-node reserved pool for Quantargo pilot (ops).
2) Engineering time to implement and smoke-test the KV prefix caching config and autoscale policy (estimate: 2 engineer-days + 1 day of perf testing).
3) Ops to author a failover runbook with automated steps and an SRE pre-warm checklist (estimate: 3 full SRE-days).

If approved I can prioritize the perf tests and put up a short runbook draft by Tue 5/5. Caveats: if Quantargo insists on 7B quantized to save cost, p95 guarantee will require additional capacity commitments from them.

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Sullivan <kate@quantargo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Quantargo Legal <legal@quantargo.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Tighter uptime/latency guarantees for pilot — proposal and next steps

Kate — quick update from our side after internal alignment: 

What we can commit for a 6-month pilot (subject to final signoff & reserved-pool provisioning):
- Measurement: canonical metric = api.p95_token_latency.us-west, measured over 5-minute windows.
- Latency: p95 <= 80ms on fp16 13B variant with a dedicated 2-node reserved pool and KV prefix caching enabled. (If Quantargo chooses 7B quantized, we will need a higher reserved concurrency to hit p95 <= 80ms.)
- Uptime: operational target 99.95% monthly for the dedicated pool during the pilot. Contractual SLA credit structure: pro-rated service credits starting at 5% for monthly uptime <99.95% and escalations per our standard template (we will draft exact language).
- Failover: warm-standby in us-east with health-check-driven routing; target RTO for region failover ~60s. Ops will provide a runbook and an SRE pre-warm checklist.

Next steps: 
1) Quantargo to confirm model preference (13B fp16 vs 7B quantized) and commitment level.
2) Redwood to provision the 2-node reserved pool and perform perf validation (ETA: perf validation by Tue 5/11).
3) Legal/Finance to circulate pilot order and proposed credit clause (Rafael to start the draft).

I'm attaching the initial runbook stub and the SLO request you shared for convenience. Rafael will follow up with a formal proposal and HS-34921 has been updated.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft-moprunbook.md; quantargo-slo-request.pdf
